147:- Change Account in the `⚙` menu (v91.0, real `claude auth` calls in v112.0, WSL support in v113.0): the one 🤖-menu feature that got a real native implementation instead of being hidden. `ChangeAccountNativeMenuItem`/`ChangeAccountNativeSeparator` (own item, not the terminal's `ChangeAccountMenuItem`) are shown by `ProviderContextMenu_Opened` only when `IsNativeModeActive && IsClaudeProvider(...)`. `ChangeAccountNativeMenuItem_Click` (NativeChat.cs) can't script `/logout` into a TUI that doesn't exist headless — measured: the headless CLI rejects slash commands sent over the structured channel outright (`AskSideQuestionAsync`'s `/btw` comment: *"isn't available in this environment"*). The v91.0 fix opened `https://claude.ai` in the default browser and relied on the user switching there, but that never actually worked: a browser session against the web app is a completely separate credential store from the one the locally-run CLI authenticates with, so the relaunch always came back on the same cached account (issue reported as "switching doesn't work"). v112.0 replaces the browser-homepage step with the CLI's own non-interactive `claude auth logout` (awaited, clears the real local credential) followed by `claude auth login` (fire-and-forget — it drives its own OAuth round-trip in the browser and isn't killed by disposing the `Process` wrapper without `Kill()`). v112.0 shipped this unconditionally against `ResolveNativeClaudeExecutable()` (the Windows-side `claude.exe`) even for the `ClaudeCodeWSL` provider — but a native-mode `ClaudeCodeWSL` session's actual child process is `wsl.exe` (`ClaudeCommandBuilder.GetFileName`), authenticating against the distro's own `~/.claude.json`, a completely separate file from the Windows one. So the v112.0 handler logged out/in a Windows credential the running WSL conversation never used: no error, but the switch silently did nothing for WSL. v113.0 fixes this by branching on `isWsl = activeProvider == AiProvider.ClaudeCodeWSL` and running both subcommands as `wsl.exe bash -lic "claude auth logout"` / `"claude auth login"` instead. Still signs out the usage WebView2 first (`SignOutUsageWindowIfActiveAsync`, same as the terminal flow) and still waits for an OK on a message box before calling `RelaunchNativeSessionAsync` so the next turn's process launch picks up whatever credentials are current at that point. `auth login` needs a real console, unlike `auth logout` (also fixed v113.0): `claude auth login` drives an interactive OAuth round-trip — it prints the browser URL to stdout and, if the browser's own redirect can't complete automatically, asks the user to paste a code back into that same process's stdin. The original v112.0 `Process.Start` used `CreateNoWindow = true` for both subcommands; `auth logout` does no interactive I/O so that was harmless, but for `auth login` it meant the process had no console at all — no stdout to print the browser URL/prompt to, no stdin to read a pasted code from — so the browser never opened and login could never actually complete, even though the `Process.Start` call itself raised no exception (reported: "browser is not opening", "not showing new account after OK", "even a new chat doesn't show the account" — all three were downstream of this one root cause, since the account was never actually being set). Fixed by launching it through `cmd.exe /k` with `CreateNoWindow = false` (`cmd.exe /k "<claudeExe>" auth login`, or `cmd.exe /k wsl bash -lic "claude auth login"` for WSL) — the same `/k`-wrapped visible-console pattern the terminal launch itself uses elsewhere in `ClaudeCodeControl.Terminal.cs`, which gives the CLI a real window to print to and read from, and keeps that window open after the CLI exits so an error stays legible instead of flashing shut. `claude.ai` is opened in the browser again too, but before `auth login` now, not instead of it (v113.0): fixing the console alone was not enough — claude.ai's OAuth *authorize* endpoint has no account picker, so if the browser is already signed in as the old account, the CLI's login round-trip silently re-approves that same account through the existing session cookies, which is indistinguishable from "the switch did nothing". So the handler now opens plain `https://claude.ai` first and blocks on a message box asking the user to consciously sign out and into the desired account there — only after that confirmation does it run `claude auth login`, which then rides whatever account is now active in the browser. A second message box (reworded from the original "browser will open" text, since the browser step already happened) asks for confirmation once the CLI's own console-window flow (paste-a-code fallback included) is done, before `RelaunchNativeSessionAsync` fires
288:- Returning to the usage view after a manual account switch (v158.0): `TryRedirectToUsage`'s post-auth landing whitelist (`/new`, `/chats`, `/chat/`, `/projects`, `/recents`) deliberately excluded the root path, because `/` doubles as the signed-out home page and redirecting it unconditionally loops `/settings/usage → / → /settings/usage`. claude.ai drops a fresh sign-in on `/` about as often as on `/new`, so Switch Account → native "Log out" → sign in as a different user left the panel parked on the home page until the user pressed Refresh. `_sawSignedOutPage` (set whenever the embedded page visits `/login`, `/logout`, `/magic-link` or `/auth`) now promotes `/` to a landing, and `RedirectToUsageIfSettledAsync` requires a non-empty claude.ai `sessionKey` cookie (`HasClaudeSessionCookieAsync`) before navigating — a genuinely signed-out root reads no cookie and is left alone. The flag is cleared as the redirect fires, so a navigate that bounces straight back to `/` cannot re-arm it: one attempt per sign-out. The settle path re-checks `core.Source` both before and after the awaited cookie read, since the await gives the page another chance to move. `/onboarding` is deliberately *not* a landing — an account claude.ai forces through onboarding would ping-pong `/onboarding → /settings/usage` every ~6.5 s (1.5 s settle + 5 s debounce).
289:- Trim restore after Switch Account (`TryRestoreTrim`, v158.0): `SwitchAccountButton_Click` sets `window.__claudeSuppressTrim` so claude.ai's own chrome — and with it the account menu — stays visible. That flag lives on the document, so a full page load clears it by itself, but an SPA route change back to `/settings/usage` does not, leaving the raw settings page (sidebar and all) in the panel. Both `OnNavigationCompleted` and `OnSourceChanged` now clear the flag whenever the source is on `/settings/usage`, ahead of the redirect check.
290:- Following a Claude CLI account switch (v221.0): the bars come from the WebView2's own claude.ai session, which has nothing to do with the CLI's credentials, so `/logout` + `/login` typed into the terminal (or `claude auth login` anywhere) moved the agent to another account while the bars kept scraping, and refreshing, the old one. Only the ⚙ "Change Account" items signed the page out. `SyncUsageWithClaudeAccountAsync` runs on every background tick (ahead of the foreground-tab guard) and once before the startup refresh. It reads `oauthAccount` from the active side's `~/.claude.json` (the distro's copy for `ClaudeCodeWSL`, with the `wslpath` result cached per session). `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is honored on both sides (`GetClaudeJsonPath`, `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME}` under WSL), because the CLI then keeps the file in that folder and never writes the one in the home directory. It identifies the account as `accountUuid/organizationUuid`, so switching organizations under the same login counts as a switch too, since usage limits are per organization. It falls back to the e-mail address when the UUIDs are missing. No `oauthAccount` (between `/logout` and `/login`) or a half-written file reads as "unknown" and never as a switch. The account the page was last paired with is kept per side (`windows`/`wsl`) in `usage-account.json` next to the settings, not in the settings. Every VS window saves its whole in-memory settings on each scrape, so a second window would write the old account back and then sign the shared page out a second time. The first check on a side only records the account. A window can find the pairing already moved to the account it now reads, because another window handled the switch. It then only drops its own cached snapshot (`_usageAccountSeen`), since its bars would otherwise sit on the old numbers until the next successful scrape. A change calls `SignOutUsageWindowIfActiveAsync(pairedAccount)`, which clears the cached snapshot, signs the page out and shows a main-window info bar (`InfoBarSlot.UsageAccount`) with an "Open Claude Usage" link. It deliberately does not pop the tab, which could steal focus while the user types. The Change Account menu items pass no account, which forgets the pairing, so the CLI login that follows is adopted silently instead of being handled as a second switch.
296:- Settings-as-dialog route (v300.0): claude.ai now redirects `/settings/usage` to `/new#settings/usage` and draws settings as a fixed `role=dialog` (`cds-dialog-regions`, a grid capped at `max-height:800px`) over the chat page. Every check that compared the *path* with `/settings/usage` failed there, so `TryRedirectToUsage` took `/new` for a post-auth landing and navigated back to the usage URL every ~6.5 s (1.5 s settle + 5 s throttle) — the "keeps refreshing" report — and `TryRestoreTrim`/Refresh misjudged the page too. `ClaudeUsagePage.IsUsagePage(Uri)` (pure, `Models/ClaudeCodeModels.cs`, unit-tested) accepts either the path or the `#settings/usage` fragment and is used everywhere the C# side asks "is this the usage view"; `ClaudeUsagePage.IsAuthPath` holds the `/login`/`/logout`/`/magic-link`/`/auth` prefixes. The injected script has its own `isUsagePage()` (pathname or hash): it trims and posts snapshots only there, so a `/new` page is never trimmed or scraped. 147:- Change Account in the `⚙` menu (v91.0, real `claude auth` calls in v112.0, WSL support in v113.0): the one 🤖-menu feature that got a real native implementation instead of being hidden. `ChangeAccountNativeMenuItem`/`ChangeAccountNativeSeparator` (own item, not the terminal's `ChangeAccountMenuItem`) are shown by `ProviderContextMenu_Opened` only when `IsNativeModeActive && IsClaudeProvider(...)`. `ChangeAccountNativeMenuItem_Click` (NativeChat.cs) can't script `/logout` into a TUI that doesn't exist headless — measured: the headless CLI rejects slash commands sent over the structured channel outright (`AskSideQuestionAsync`'s `/btw` comment: *"isn't available in this environment"*). The v91.0 fix opened `https://claude.ai` in the default browser and relied on the user switching there, but that never actually worked: a browser session against the web app is a completely separate credential store from the one the locally-run CLI authenticates with, so the relaunch always came back on the same cached account (issue reported as "switching doesn't work"). v112.0 replaces the browser-homepage step with the CLI's own non-interactive `claude auth logout` (awaited, clears the real local credential) followed by `claude auth login` (fire-and-forget — it drives its own OAuth round-trip in the browser and isn't killed by disposing the `Process` wrapper without `Kill()`). v112.0 shipped this unconditionally against `ResolveNativeClaudeExecutable()` (the Windows-side `claude.exe`) even for the `ClaudeCodeWSL` provider — but a native-mode `ClaudeCodeWSL` session's actual child process is `wsl.exe` (`ClaudeCommandBuilder.GetFileName`), authenticating against the distro's own `~/.claude.json`, a completely separate file from the Windows one. So the v112.0 handler logged out/in a Windows credential the running WSL conversation never used: no error, but the switch silently did nothing for WSL. v113.0 fixes this by branching on `isWsl = activeProvider == AiProvider.ClaudeCodeWSL` and running both subcommands as `wsl.exe bash -lic "claude auth logout"` / `"claude auth login"` instead. Still signs out the usage WebView2 first (`SignOutUsageWindowIfActiveAsync`, same as the terminal flow) and still waits for an OK on a message box before calling `RelaunchNativeSessionAsync` so the next turn's process launch picks up whatever credentials are current at that point. `auth login` needs a real console, unlike `auth logout` (also fixed v113.0): `claude auth login` drives an interactive OAuth round-trip — it prints the browser URL to stdout and, if the browser's own redirect can't complete automatically, asks the user to paste a code back into that same process's stdin. The original v112.0 `Process.Start` used `CreateNoWindow = true` for both subcommands; `auth logout` does no interactive I/O so that was harmless, but for `auth login` it meant the process had no console at all — no stdout to print the browser URL/prompt to, no stdin to read a pasted code from — so the browser never opened and login could never actually complete, even though the `Process.Start` call itself raised no exception (reported: "browser is not opening", "not showing new account after OK", "even a new chat doesn't show the account" — all three were downstream of this one root cause, since the account was never actually being set). Fixed by launching it through `cmd.exe /k` with `CreateNoWindow = false` (`cmd.exe /k "<claudeExe>" auth login`, or `cmd.exe /k wsl bash -lic "claude auth login"` for WSL) — the same `/k`-wrapped visible-console pattern the terminal launch itself uses elsewhere in `ClaudeCodeControl.Terminal.cs`, which gives the CLI a real window to print to and read from, and keeps that window open after the CLI exits so an error stays legible instead of flashing shut. `claude.ai` is opened in the browser again too, but before `auth login` now, not instead of it (v113.0): fixing the console alone was not enough — claude.ai's OAuth *authorize* endpoint has no account picker, so if the browser is already signed in as the old account, the CLI's login round-trip silently re-approves that same account through the existing session cookies, which is indistinguishable from "the switch did nothing". So the handler now opens plain `https://claude.ai` first and blocks on a message box asking the user to consciously sign out and into the desired account there — only after that confirmation does it run `claude auth login`, which then rides whatever account is now active in the browser. A second message box (reworded from the original "browser will open" text, since the browser step already happened) asks for confirmation once the CLI's own console-window flow (paste-a-code fallback included) is done, before `RelaunchNativeSessionAsync` fires
288:- Returning to the usage view after a manual account switch (v158.0): `TryRedirectToUsage`'s post-auth landing whitelist (`/new`, `/chats`, `/chat/`, `/projects`, `/recents`) deliberately excluded the root path, because `/` doubles as the signed-out home page and redirecting it unconditionally loops `/settings/usage → / → /settings/usage`. claude.ai drops a fresh sign-in on `/` about as often as on `/new`, so Switch Account → native "Log out" → sign in as a different user left the panel parked on the home page until the user pressed Refresh. `_sawSignedOutPage` (set whenever the embedded page visits `/login`, `/logout`, `/magic-link` or `/auth`) now promotes `/` to a landing, and `RedirectToUsageIfSettledAsync` requires a non-empty claude.ai `sessionKey` cookie (`HasClaudeSessionCookieAsync`) before navigating — a genuinely signed-out root reads no cookie and is left alone. The flag is cleared as the redirect fires, so a navigate that bounces straight back to `/` cannot re-arm it: one attempt per sign-out. The settle path re-checks `core.Source` both before and after the awaited cookie read, since the await gives the page another chance to move. `/onboarding` is deliberately *not* a landing — an account claude.ai forces through onboarding would ping-pong `/onboarding → /settings/usage` every ~6.5 s (1.5 s settle + 5 s debounce).
289:- Trim restore after Switch Account (`TryRestoreTrim`, v158.0): `SwitchAccountButton_Click` sets `window.__claudeSuppressTrim` so claude.ai's own chrome — and with it the account menu — stays visible. That flag lives on the document, so a full page load clears it by itself, but an SPA route change back to `/settings/usage` does not, leaving the raw settings page (sidebar and all) in the panel. Both `OnNavigationCompleted` and `OnSourceChanged` now clear the flag whenever the source is on `/settings/usage`, ahead of the redirect check.
290:- Following a Claude CLI account switch (v221.0): the bars come from the WebView2's own claude.ai session, which has nothing to do with the CLI's credentials, so `/logout` + `/login` typed into the terminal (or `claude auth login` anywhere) moved the agent to another account while the bars kept scraping, and refreshing, the old one. Only the ⚙ "Change Account" items signed the page out. `SyncUsageWithClaudeAccountAsync` runs on every background tick (ahead of the foreground-tab guard) and once before the startup refresh. It reads `oauthAccount` from the active side's `~/.claude.json` (the distro's copy for `ClaudeCodeWSL`, with the `wslpath` result cached per session). `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is honored on both sides (`GetClaudeJsonPath`, `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME}` under WSL), because the CLI then keeps the file in that folder and never writes the one in the home directory. It identifies the account as `accountUuid/organizationUuid`, so switching organizations under the same login counts as a switch too, since usage limits are per organization. It falls back to the e-mail address when the UUIDs are missing. No `oauthAccount` (between `/logout` and `/login`) or a half-written file reads as "unknown" and never as a switch. Every VS window saves its whole in-memory settings on each scrape, so a second window would write the old account back and then sign the shared page out a second time. The first check on a side only records the account. A window can find the pairing already moved to the account it now reads, because another window handled the switch. It then only drops its own cached snapshot (`_usageAccountSeen`), since its bars would otherwise sit on the old numbers until the next successful scrape. content.text:
Publiquei a versão 302.0 no Marketplace. O "Trocar de conta" agora deve deixar o "Continuar com o Google" habilitado também na versão instalada, mas isso ainda não foi testado lá.

**O que era:** o código era o mesmo, o que mudava era o navegador embutido da aba de uso:
- Com o VS normal aberto, a pasta de perfil fica travada por ele. Por isso o Exp abriu numa pasta de perfil nova e vazia, e lá tudo funcionava.
- A versão instalada usa o perfil antigo. Ele ainda guarda o estado de "adicionar conta" do claude.ai, deixado pelo "Trocar de conta" da v300. Esse estado mantém o botão do Google cinza mesmo depois do logout da v301.

**A correção:** antes de sair, o "Trocar de conta" apaga os cookies e os dados salvos só do claude.ai e do anthropic.com. Os cookies do Google ficam, então a sua conta Google continua lembrada.

**O que foi verificado:**
- No Edge headless, conferi que a limpeza apaga os dados salvos do claude.ai. Mas ela deixa alguns cookies para trás, por isso o código também apaga os cookies diretamente.
- Os 1086 testes passaram, o build Release foi feito e a publicação deu certo. O commit `4412527` já está no master.
- Não consegui reproduzir o seu caso exato: o arquivo de cookies do perfil fica travado enquanto o VS está aberto.

**Para testar:** atualize a extensão, abra o Uso do Claude e clique em **Trocar de conta** de novo. A limpeza acontece no clique.

Se o Google continuar cinza, clique em **Sair**, que apaga todos os dados do navegador embutido, inclusive os do Google. Se assim funcionar, a causa está nos cookies do próprio Google, e eu ajusto o "Trocar de conta" para limpar esses também.

+- *Switch Account* in Claude Usage now fully resets the embedded browser before the login screen, so "Continue with Google" is no longer greyed out (you sign in to Google again there).
- *Switch Account* in Claude Usage no longer leaves "Continue with Google" greyed out in an installation that had used the old account switcher; your Google sign-in is kept.

<Description xml:space="preserve">Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Open Code, Devin, PI, Antigravity, Reasonix, Qwen Code, Grok in Visual Studio. Image/file paste, diff viewer, on-finish actions, usage tracking, session history and more</Description>

- Follow-up — the `keep` rule was the same bug (v73.0): the ancestor-side fix alone didn't restore scrolling, because `findIsolationTarget()` can resolve to a `tabindex=-1` dialog shell (not just the small `div.pb-8` block) when the page has one — that shell itself commonly uses `display:flex; flex-direction:column` to stack a header above the internally-scrolling body. The `[data-claude-usage-keep="1"]` rule was still forcing `display:block !important` on the target, which collapses that flex-column and strips the scrollable child's bounded height (its `flex-1`/`min-h-0` become no-ops once the parent isn't a flex container) — the shell's own untouched `overflow:hidden` then just clips the excess with no scrollbar, no matter what the ancestor-side fix does. `keep` now only widens the target (`width`/`max-width`/`margin`/`box-sizing`) and leaves `display`/`height`/`overflow`/`padding` completely alone, same principle as the `scrollbox` rule.

- Docked tab painting over its neighbour (v230.0): the WebView2 is a native child window, so WPF clipping and z-order never apply to it. Measured on a tab docked in the document well with the Output pane below: the control's bottom edge landed at the bottom of the Output pane, i.e. it was laid out ~280 px taller than the area the shell shows, so the shell clipped the WPF elements (status bar) while the native window kept painting over Output. `ClaudeUsageControl`'s guard (`#region WebView2 bounds guard`) runs 150 ms after `SizeChanged`/`IsVisibleChanged`/the frame's `OnSize`, and on a 2 s heartbeat while the control is loaded. (1) `ClampWebViewToVisibleArea` hit-tests the `WebArea` grid (it has a `Transparent` background on purpose — WPF hit testing skips an element with no brush) down its middle: WPF hit testing honors the shell's clip, so the first point that no longer hits one of this control's own visuals is where the pane ends (one hit test when nothing is cut off, a ~7-step binary search otherwise). The web view host then gets an explicit `Height` of the visible part with `VerticalAlignment=Top` (not `MaxHeight`: a non-stretched host sizes to its content and an `HwndHost` desires 0); the clamp is released when the area is fully visible again. (2) `RepairWebViewBounds` compares `GetWindowRect(WebView.Handle)` with where WPF put the element (`PointToScreen` + `ActualWidth/Height` × the DPI transform) through the pure `HostedWindowBounds.IsMisaligned` (2 px tolerance, an element with no area never counts); a mismatch must be seen on two consecutive checks before anything is done, then `NudgeWebViewLayout` (width −1 px and back), and if the window is still wrong `SnapWindowTo` (`SetWindowPos`). Three failed repairs in a row back it off for 60 s. The off-screen scraper is skipped. Diagnostics: every change of state is appended to `%LocalAppData%\ClaudeCodeExtension\usage-layout.log` (control/area size, visible height, the frame's own `GetFramePos`, and — only while clipped — the ancestor chain with each element's vertical extent and clip flags; restarted past 200 KB). If the overlap ever returns, that file says whether WPF's layout, the shell's clip or the window itself is the one that is off.

- Settings-as-dialog route (v300.0): claude.ai now redirects `/settings/usage` to `/new#settings/usage` and draws settings as a fixed `role=dialog` (`cds-dialog-regions`, a grid capped at `max-height:800px`) over the chat page. Every check that compared the *path* with `/settings/usage` failed there, so `TryRedirectToUsage` took `/new` for a post-auth landing and navigated back to the usage URL every ~6.5 s (1.5 s settle + 5 s throttle) — the "keeps refreshing" report — and `TryRestoreTrim`/Refresh misjudged the page too. `ClaudeUsagePage.IsUsagePage(Uri)` (pure, `Models/ClaudeCodeModels.cs`, unit-tested) accepts either the path or the `#settings/usage` fragment and is used everywhere the C# side asks "is this the usage view"; `ClaudeUsagePage.IsAuthPath` holds the `/login`/`/logout`/`/magic-link`/`/auth` prefixes. The injected script has its own `isUsagePage()` (pathname or hash): it trims and posts snapshots only there, so a `/new` page is never trimmed or scraped. Layout: the trim CSS stretches the kept dialog to the whole viewport (`position:fixed; inset:0; max-height:none; border-radius:0; grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr)`) and hides its title row (`.col-span-full.row-start-1`, which holds claude.ai's X — closing it would leave the bare chat page); the dialog's own `overflow-y-auto` pane keeps scrolling to the end. Verified live in Edge with the extension's cookies at 1142×616.

-- Switch Account (v301.0, replaces the v300.0 account-menu flow): `SwitchAccountButton_Click` deletes the shared cookie copy (`SharedCookiePath`, which would sign a rebuilt view back in as the same account), resets `_lastCookieSaveUtc` and navigates to `LogoutUrl` (`https://claude.ai/logout`, the `href` of claude.ai's own "Log out" menu item). `/logout` is an auth path, so `_sawSignedOutPage` is set and `TryRedirectToUsage` brings the usage view back after the next sign-in. Unlike Sign out (`SignOutAsync`, which clears all site data), the Google session stays, so Google sign-in offers the accounts it knows. With no live core it falls back to `SignOutAsync`. v302.0: before navigating, `ClearClaudeSiteDataAsync` deletes every cookie whose domain is claude.ai/anthropic.com (`ClaudeUsagePage.IsClaudeSiteCookieDomain`, from `CookieManager.GetCookiesAsync(null)`) and runs CDP `Storage.clearDataForOrigin` (`storageTypes: all`) for `ClaudeUsagePage.ClaudeSiteOrigins`. The v301.0 plain `/logout` worked in the Exp instance but not in the installed one: the Exp instance got the per-PID fallback folder (`WebView2_<pid>`, the installed VS held the shared `WebView2` folder), i.e. a fresh profile, while the long-lived profile still carried claude.ai's add-account state from the v300.0 flow and kept Google greyed after logout. Google's own cookies are not touched. Why the v300.0 flow was dropped: it opened claude.ai's account menu (`[data-testid="user-menu-button"]` on `/new`) and the user's "add account" path from there is claude.ai's add/switch-account login, which locks the e-mail and disables "Continue with Google" (`disabled` when that flow is active). The switch-mode state (`_switchAccountMode`, timer, cookie signature poll, `Reload()`/redirect exceptions) went with it.

+- Switch Account (v301.0, replaces the v300.0 account-menu flow): `SwitchAccountButton_Click` deletes the shared cookie copy (`SharedCookiePath`, which would sign a rebuilt view back in as the same account), resets `_lastCookieSaveUtc` and navigates to `LogoutUrl` (`https://claude.ai/logout`, the `href` of claude.ai's own "Log out" menu item). `/logout` is an auth path, so `_sawSignedOutPage` is set and `TryRedirectToUsage` brings the usage view back after the next sign-in. Unlike Sign out (`SignOutAsync`, which clears all site data), the Google session stays, so Google sign-in offers the accounts it knows. With no live core it falls back to `SignOutAsync`. v303.0: before navigating it wipes the whole profile (`ClearSessionDataAsync(core, wholeProfile: true)` → `CoreWebView2BrowsingDataKinds.AllProfile`, Google's session included). History: v301.0 (plain `/logout`) worked in the Exp instance only because Exp got the per-PID fallback folder (`WebView2_<pid>`; the installed VS held the shared `WebView2` folder), i.e. a brand-new profile. v302.0 cleared only claude.ai/anthropic.com cookies and storage — the login page came back in its full signed-out layout, yet Google stayed greyed — so the leftover state is outside claude.ai (Google's own session is the prime suspect) and only a profile as clean as a new one was ever seen to work. The "Unlike Sign out ... the Google session stays" note above no longer holds. Why the v300.0 flow was dropped: it opened claude.ai's account menu (`[data-testid="user-menu-button"]` on `/new`) and the user's "add account" path from there is claude.ai's add/switch-account login, which locks the e-mail and disables "Continue with Google" (`disabled` when that flow is active). The switch-mode state (`_switchAccountMode`, timer, cookie signature poll, `Reload()`/redirect exceptions) went with it.

- Native-mode composer usage button (v235.0, `Controls/ClaudeCodeControl.ChatUsageIndicator.cs`, `UI/ChatUsageIndicator.cs`, `UI/ChatTranscriptView.xaml` `ComposerUsageButton`/`UsagePopup`): a ring after the composer's Permissions selector, shown only for Claude providers. The popup has two halves: the context window of the chat's last completed turn (`ClaudeStatusLineInput` captured in `CompleteNativeTurn`/`CompleteNativeTurnForSession` into `_mainStatusLine` or `NativeChatSessionState.LastStatusLine`, cleared by Clear Chat), and the plan limits read from the cached `LastUsageJson` (the same numbers as the inline bars, so `NoWeeklyLimit`/`HasExtraUsage` are honored). The ring fills with context %, or with the session limit before any turn has reported a window. `HandleScrapedSnapshot` calls `RefreshChatUsageIndicators()`, so an open popup updates in place. Opening the popup raises `UsageRequested`, handled by `RefreshUsageForIndicatorAsync`: the same account-switch guard the background timer uses first, then `Reload()` when the tab is visible, otherwise `EnsureUsageToolWindowAsync(showWindow:false, updateWindowState:false, activate:false)`, so the tab never appears from a ring click. "See detailed breakdown" (`UsageDetailsRequested`) calls `EnsureUsageToolWindowAsync(showWindow:true)`, the same as the inline bars. The popup's "Updated / Not updated since" line uses `IsUsageSnapshotStale`. Formatting and ring geometry are pure (`ChatUsageIndicator`, unit-tested in `Tests/ChatUsageIndicatorTests.cs`). Popup rows (v236.0): label column `Auto`, value column `*` right-aligned with `CharacterEllipsis`; the border is `MinWidth=280`/`MaxWidth=440` instead of a fixed 280, because a long value ("0% used · Starts with your first message") in the old `*`/`Auto` layout squeezed the label column and drew over "Current session". `UsageNoPlanText` keeps `MaxWidth=256` so its wrapping does not stretch the popup. "Refreshing…" (v236.0): a ring click sets the view's `_usageRefreshing`, so the last line reads "Refreshing…" (snapshot pushes in the meantime only update the stored `_usageUpdatedText`) until the control calls `EndUsageRefresh()` on the clicked transcript when `RefreshUsageForIndicatorAsync` finishes. That task waits for real data: the off-screen path through `RefreshUsageInBackgroundAsync`'s own wait, the visible-tab `Reload()` path on `_indicatorScrapeTcs` (completed in `HandleScrapedSnapshot`, 15 s cap). A click while one is running joins the running `_indicatorRefresh` instead of starting another. Not F5-verified. The popup's wait is capped at `UsageRefreshTextCapMs` (20 s, v268.0): the off-screen path can chain a 10 s silent reload, a WebView2 rebuild (up to 30 s) and another 10 s wait, so "Refreshing…" could sit there over a minute after a fresh sign-in; the refresh itself keeps running and a later snapshot still updates the popup in place. Refresh ring (v276.0): the last line no longer swaps to "Refreshing…" (which hid the time); `UsageUpdatedRow` keeps the "Updated" text and shows `UsageRefreshSpinner` (10 px ring, tooltip "Refreshing…") beside it while `_usageRefreshing`. The rotation is started/stopped with `BeginAnimation` in `ShowUsageUpdatedText` only when the state flips, never by a style trigger (the v265.0 crash). Account line (v300.0, source changed in v301.0): the e-mail is the Claude CLI's own account, not the usage page's claude.ai login (the two can differ). `GetClaudeCliAccountIdAsync` (run by every `SyncUsageWithClaudeAccountAsync`: startup, background refresh, ring click) reads `.claude.json` once and also stores `oauthAccount.emailAddress` (`ParseClaudeAccountEmail`) per side (`windows`/`wsl`) in `_claudeCliAccountEmails`, re-pushing the indicators when it changes; `BuildChatUsageIndicatorData` takes it from `GetClaudeCliAccountEmail(provider)`, whether or not a snapshot exists. `UsageSnapshot.AccountEmail` (from the injected script's `/api/account` fetch) is still recorded but no longer shown and `UsageAccountText` at the bottom of the popup shows "Account: {0}" (collapsed when empty, e.g. a snapshot cached by an older version). `RefreshLanguage` redoes it.

- Icon-font glyphs in reset text (v268.0): claude.ai renders some icons as Private Use Area characters, and on some rows (seen on the Italian weekly row) the only `.text-secondary` element of the label column holds such an icon instead of a reset date, so `readLabelAndReset` took `U+E027` as `WeeklyReset` and VS drew it as a box. The scraper now strips `U+E000–U+F8FF` before choosing the reset text; `ChatUsageIndicator.StripIconGlyphs` does the same on the C# side (popup rows via `PlanRowText`, inline reset labels) so snapshots cached before the fix render clean too.
